card.line: Samaria was the hill city Omri built as the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel, a place of evil kings that finally fell to Assyria.

moments.title: Omri builds Samaria
moments.text: Omri paid Shemer two talents of silver for the hill of Samaria and built a city on it. He named the city after Shemer, who had owned the hill.

moments.title: Ahab's temple of Baal
moments.text: Ahab became king and reigned in Samaria twenty-two years. He married Jezebel and built a temple for Baal in Samaria, where he set up an altar for Baal.

moments.title: Blind soldiers led to Samaria
moments.text: Elisha prayed and God struck the Aramean soldiers with blindness. Elisha led them into Samaria, where God opened their eyes, and the king fed them and sent them home.

moments.title: Famine under siege
moments.text: Ben-hadad of Aram surrounded Samaria with his army, and a terrible famine followed. Food became so costly that a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver.

moments.title: Assyria captures Samaria
moments.text: Assyria's king besieged Samaria for three years and then captured it. He carried the Israelites away to Assyria because they had sinned against the LORD.
